Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: List has been revised.
No one is present on behalf of the complainant.

2. Heard Sri Ramesh Kumar, learned counsel for applicant and Sri Rajesh Kumar Srivastava,
learned A.G.A. for the State.
3.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No. 152 of 2018, under Sections 363, 366, 328, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Madawara, District Lalitpur with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

4. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have enticed away the minor niece of the informant on 8.8.2018 and is stated to have rendered her unconscious by administering some obnoxious material to her.
The victim is stated to have been taken far away to Indore by the applicant.

entities.text: Arvind vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The FIR is delayed by three days and there is no explanation for said delay caused and as such abscondance was not reported anywhere by the informant.
Learned counsel has further stated that injury report does not corroborate the prosecution story of sexual assault.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents to his credit.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 11.8.2018.

6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the victim was minor at the time of offence and her age as per ossification test is also 16 years, whereby even her consent becomes insignificant.
Learned AGA has further stated that statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. of the victim categorically states that the applicant sexually assaulted her without her consent.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties, going through the evidence on record and taking into consideration the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and the medical record, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
8. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.

9. However, it is directed that the court below may proceed with the trial and reach at the logical conclusion expeditiously, if there is no legal impediment, within a period of one year from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.

10. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 20.1.2023 Vikas  Arvind vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188660254/
